recent_posts.title: 12 companies share real data on 4 day work weeks for developers
recent_posts.summary: Analysis of 12 companies implementing 4-day work weeks for development teams shows significant productivity gains (15-40% increases), improved developer satisfaction, and reduced burnout. Companies like Buffer, Basecamp, and Microsoft Japan reported faster feature delivery, better code quality, and higher retention rates. Success requires proper project management tools, clear communication protocols, and outcome-based metrics rather than time-based measurements. The compressed schedule works well for developers due to their need for deep work and focus time.

recent_posts.title: Approximating Named Arguments in Java
recent_posts.summary: Java lacks native named arguments and default parameter values, forcing developers to use workarounds like the builder pattern, public field classes, or records. Each approach has trade-offs: builders require boilerplate, mutable objects are hard to reason about, and records have constructor limitations. The builder pattern creates both input and mutable intermediate classes, while public fields risk mutability issues. Records offer immutability but lack convenient withers (not yet in Java). The classic object-oriented approach of "make it, tweak it, run it" provides another alternative. Future withers support in records shows the most promise for approximating named arguments effectively.

recent_posts.title: Preparing for Spring Boot 4 and Spring Framework 7: What’s New?
recent_posts.summary: Spring Boot 4 and Spring Framework 7 are major upcoming releases scheduled for 2025 that modernize Java development. Spring Framework 7 introduces built-in resilience features with annotations like @Retryable and @ConcurrencyLimit, enhanced API versioning support, Jakarta EE 11 compatibility, and requires JDK 17+ with JDK 25 recommended. Spring Boot 4 features modular architecture for smaller JARs, mandates Java 17+ baseline, integrates Micrometer 2.0 for better observability, and improves GraalVM native image performance. Both versions adopt JSpecify annotations for null safety, support Jackson 3.x, and focus on developer productivity improvements while maintaining compatibility with modern servlet containers.

recent_posts.title: From Final to Immutable: The not-so-final word on `final` #JVMLS
recent_posts.summary: Java's final fields provide immutability benefits like safe sharing across threads and composition without defensive copying, but they're not truly final due to reflection-based mutation and constructor visibility issues. The JVM can't fully optimize final field access because of these limitations. Project Valhalla introduces strict final fields that can only be initialized before superclass constructor calls, enabling better optimization. For lazy initialization scenarios, final fields are too restrictive, leading to the development of the stable value API in Java 25, which provides atomic at-most-once mutation semantics while maintaining performance optimization capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Refactoring at Scale with José Calderón
recent_posts.summary: José Calderón, lead software engineer at JP Morgan Chase, discusses his journey from fixing computers as a child to becoming an enterprise Java developer. He shares insights on refactoring versus rewriting legacy systems, emphasizing the importance of documenting architectural decisions through ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) stored in source control. The conversation covers testing strategies including synthetic testing for event-driven systems, database abstraction with tools like Liquibase, and the evolving role of AI in software development. José advocates for maintaining evolutionary architecture through careful decision tracking and argues that developers using AI tools will outperform those who don't.

recent_posts.title: How developers can build profitable micro SaaS products in 2025
recent_posts.summary: Developers can transition from traditional freelancing to building micro-SaaS products using the 'Build Once, Sell Forever' model. This approach involves creating small, automated tools that solve specific problems and generate recurring revenue. A recommended tech stack includes Next.js, Supabase, Tailwind CSS, and Stripe, allowing developers to launch products within 48 hours. The strategy focuses on building multiple small tools that each generate $500+ monthly rather than pursuing large startup ventures.

recent_posts.title: Minimal Scala Container Images using Nix
recent_posts.summary: A detailed guide on reducing Docker image sizes for Scala applications from 722 MB to 198 MB using Nix. The approach involves using jre_minimal instead of full JDK, analyzing dependencies with jdeps to include only necessary Java modules, and optimizing Docker image construction with buildEnv to avoid file duplication. The tutorial covers common pitfalls like missing SSL modules and provides a complete working derivation for creating minimal container images.

recent_posts.title: How to Use innerHTML, innerText, and textContent Correctly in JavaScript
recent_posts.summary: Explains the differences between three JavaScript DOM properties: innerHTML returns full HTML content with tags, innerText returns only visible styled text respecting CSS rules, and textContent returns all text content regardless of CSS visibility. Each property serves different use cases in DOM manipulation.

recent_posts.title: Happy Numbers,Trapping of Rainwater
recent_posts.summary: Two classic coding interview problems are solved in Java: Happy Numbers (determining if a number eventually reaches 1 through repeated digit squaring) and Trapping Rainwater (calculating water volume trapped between elevation bars). The Happy Numbers solution uses a HashSet to detect cycles, while the Rainwater solution employs left and right maximum arrays to find trapped water at each position.

recent_posts.title: Injecting Java from native libraries on Android
recent_posts.summary: Rust developers can inject Java classes into Android's JVM at runtime using DexClassLoader, enabling cross-platform libraries to access Android-specific APIs without requiring app developers to manually add Java helper classes. This technique involves compiling Java code to DEX format during build time and loading it dynamically through JNI, making Rust libraries more self-contained on Android.
